    • 1. 1. Purpose and Scope
    • GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE
      2.8.1. Requirement File Tree Parent Anchor GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE This requirement is the parent anchor for the approved StrictDoc child-file tree. Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-MCP-ROOT
    1.1. GHOST MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-ROOT GHOST shall provide a Model Context Protocol interface through which approved external AI clients can invoke explicitly exposed GHOST capabilities.

    The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

    MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.
    • GHOST-MCP-CHILD-DOCUMENTS
      1.2. MCP Child Requirement Documents GHOST-MCP-CHILD-DOCUMENTS The MCP capability shall be decomposed into:

      1. 111_mcp_capabilities.sdoc for all approved MCP capabilities except ActiveBlackboard.
      2. 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc for all current and future ActiveBlackboard behavior.
      3. 113_mcp_runtime_control.sdoc for MCP-visible GHOST runtime life

      The child files shall inherit from GHOST-MCP-ROOT and shall not duplicate the common protocol, authorization, transport, deployment-boundary, or client-interoperability requirements owned by this document.
    • GHOST-MCP-INTERFACE-OWNERSHIP
      1.3. MCP Interface Ownership GHOST-MCP-INTERFACE-OWNERSHIP The MCP parent capability shall own:

      - external MCP protocol behavior;
      - MCP transport requirements;
      - MCP capability negotiation;
      - tool discovery and invocation rules;
      - authenticated caller identity;
      - authorization enforcement;
      - common tool-call rate limiting;
      - interface-visible errors;
      - cross-client interoperability;
      - shared MCP security boundaries; and
      - the boundary between MCP functionality and runtime/deployment realization.

      The MCP parent capability shall not duplicate the internal algorithms of Prompt Engineering, Memory Management, ActiveBlackboard, or other GHOST functional subsystems.
      • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESSING-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE
        5.1. Prompt Processing Ownership Boundary GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESSING-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE The existing GHOST Prompt Engineering capability shall reuse the owning PreProcessing, PromptShaper, Agent Stack, SuperPrompt, and projection behavior rather than implementing duplicate prompt-processing algorithms inside the MCP transport layer.

        Detailed Prompt Engineering MCP behavior is owned by 111_mcp_capabilities.sdoc.
      • GHOST-MCP-AWS-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE
        5.2. Runtime and Deployment Ownership Boundary GHOST-MCP-AWS-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE Runtime Platform and Operations requirements shall remain responsible for:

        - local runtime realization;
        - AWS runtime realization;
        - container execution;
        - image delivery;
        - public endpoint realization;
        - HTTPS termination;
        - reverse proxy;
        - DNS;
        - authorization-provider deployment;
        - secrets delivery;
        - process startup and restart;
        - persistent deployment paths; and
        - operational verification.

        This MCP requirement family shall define what the MCP capability must do, while the 80-series requirement family shall define how the supported runtime environments deploy and operate it.
      • GHOST-MCP-UI-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY
        5.3. Human Interface Boundary GHOST-MCP-UI-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY The MCP service shall not own the native ChatGPT or Claude user interface.

        The Streamlit and future React/FastAPI interfaces remain separate GHOST interface capabilities.

        An MCP result may be rendered by the invoking client without transferring ownership of the native client UI to GHOST.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY
        5.4. Memory Infrastructure Ownership Boundary GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY MCP memory capabilities may use the common GHOST MemoryRecord, .ragmem, .ragmeta.json, SQLite, vector, and memory-management infrastructure.

        The MCP capability requirements shall define MCP-specific memory semantics without redefining unrelated GUI memory-pipeline behavior.

        Where existing Memory Management requirements remain applicable, they shall remain authoritative for their existing scope.
    • GHOST-MCP-PRODUCT-PACKAGE-BOUNDARY
      1.4. Product and Python Package Naming Boundary GHOST-MCP-PRODUCT-PACKAGE-BOUNDARY The product exposed through MCP shall be named GHOST.

      The existing Python package namespace may remain ragstream in implementation paths.

      MCP tool descriptions and client-facing metadata shall not present RAGstream as the product identity.
    • GHOST-MCP-REMOTE-TOOL-PROVIDER
      2.1. MCP Tool Provider Role GHOST-MCP-REMOTE-TOOL-PROVIDER The GHOST MCP server shall act as a tool provider.

      An external AI client shall explicitly invoke an exposed GHOST MCP operation.

      The MCP server shall not claim to passively receive, monitor, intercept, or persist ordinary client conversation traffic for which no applicable GHOST tool invocation occurs.
    • GHOST-MCP-CLIENT-COMPATIBILITY
      2.2. ChatGPT and Claude Compatibility GHOST-MCP-CLIENT-COMPATIBILITY The same GHOST MCP service contract shall be usable by approved ChatGPT and Claude MCP client integrations.

      Core GHOST semantics shall not change merely because the invoking client is ChatGPT rather than Claude.

      Client-specific user-interface behavior, connector configuration, or authentication setup may differ without creating different GHOST functional contracts.
      • GHOST-MCP-EXPLICIT-CLIENT-INVOCATION
        2.3. Explicit Client Invocation Boundary GHOST-MCP-EXPLICIT-CLIENT-INVOCATION A GHOST MCP operation shall execute only when the client issues the corresponding MCP request.

        Enabling a GHOST connector or plugin shall not by itself authorize GHOST to treat every ordinary client message as an MCP operation.
      • GHOST-MCP-CROSS-CLIENT-CONSISTENCY
        6.4. Cross-Client Functional Consistency GHOST-MCP-CROSS-CLIENT-CONSISTENCY ChatGPT and Claude shall invoke the same underlying GHOST capability semantics when they call the same MCP tool.

        Client-specific presentation or connection details shall not create different persistence, retrieval, deletion, or prompt-engineering semantics.
    • GHOST-MCP-REMOTE-STREAMABLE-HTTP
      2.4. Streamable HTTP Transport GHOST-MCP-REMOTE-STREAMABLE-HTTP The remote GHOST MCP service shall support MCP through Streamable HTTP.

      The server shall provide a logical MCP endpoint supporting the protocol operations required by the selected MCP implementation.

      Concrete hostnames, ports, reverse-proxy rules, container topology, and AWS network realization shall remain owned by the Runtime Platform and Operations requirement family.
      • GHOST-MCP-EXTERNAL-HTTPS
        2.5. Protected External HTTPS GHOST-MCP-EXTERNAL-HTTPS Remote MCP clients shall communicate with the deployed GHOST MCP endpoint through HTTPS.

        External clients shall not be required to connect directly to an unencrypted public application port or directly to an internal container port.
      • GHOST-MCP-PROTOCOL-INITIALIZATION
        2.6. MCP Initialization and Capability Negotiation GHOST-MCP-PROTOCOL-INITIALIZATION The GHOST MCP server shall support the MCP initialization exchange and shall advertise only protocol capabilities supported by the active server implementation.

        The server shall advertise tool capability when GHOST tools are available.

        Additional MCP protocol capabilities shall not be claimed merely because they exist in the MCP specification or client implementation.
        • GHOST-MCP-TOOLS-LIST
          2.7. Tool Discovery GHOST-MCP-TOOLS-LIST tools/list shall return the GHOST MCP tools currently approved and exposed by the active server implementation.

          Tool discovery shall be the authoritative client-visible inventory of callable GHOST MCP operations.

          An implementation experiment shall not automatically become a permanent GHOST requirement merely because it temporarily appears in tool metadata or code.
          • GHOST-MCP-TOOLS-CALL
            2.8. Tool Invocation GHOST-MCP-TOOLS-CALL The server shall accept tools/call only for an advertised and authorized GHOST tool.

            Before application behavior executes, the request shall pass applicable:
            - protocol validation;
            - authentication;
            - authorization;
            - rate limiting; and
            - tool-input validation.

            An unknown or undeclared tool shall not invoke GHOST application logic.
            • GHOST-MCP-TOOL-RATE-LIMITING
              4.1. Authenticated Tool Rate Limiting GHOST-MCP-TOOL-RATE-LIMITING Authenticated GHOST MCP tool invocations shall be subject to configurable rate limiting before the protected application operation executes.

              The current runtime identifies callers by authenticated owner identity.

              Concrete quotas, time windows, and deployment values shall remain deployment configuration rather than fixed functional requirements.
            • GHOST-MCP-REQUEST-ISOLATION
              4.2. Request Isolation GHOST-MCP-REQUEST-ISOLATION Concurrent MCP calls shall not accidentally exchange request-specific mutable state or tool results.

              Persistent state may be shared only through an explicitly defined persistent capability such as memory or ActiveBlackboard and only according to its owning requirements.
          • GHOST-MCP-TOOL-METADATA-TRUTH
            4.5. Tool Metadata Shall Match Behavior GHOST-MCP-TOOL-METADATA-TRUTH MCP tool metadata, including read-only, destructive, persistence, and idempotency indications, shall reflect the actual approved behavior of the corresponding operation.

            A destructive or persistent operation shall not be presented to the client as harmless or read-only.
      • GHOST-MCP-ORIGIN-VALIDATION
        3.8. Streamable HTTP Origin Validation GHOST-MCP-ORIGIN-VALIDATION The remote MCP runtime shall apply the configured transport-security policy, including Origin validation where required by the selected MCP transport implementation.

        Accepted hosts and origins are deployment values and shall remain outside the functional MCP capability requirements.
    • GHOST-MCP-PROTECTED-ACCESS
      3.1. Protected MCP Access GHOST-MCP-PROTECTED-ACCESS The deployed remote MCP service shall require authenticated access through the approved MCP-compatible OAuth authorization flow.

      An unauthenticated or invalidly authenticated remote request shall not execute a protected GHOST tool.
      • GHOST-MCP-OAUTH-PROTECTED-RESOURCE-METADATA
        3.2. OAuth Protected Resource Metadata GHOST-MCP-OAUTH-PROTECTED-RESOURCE-METADATA The protected remote GHOST MCP endpoint shall expose the OAuth Protected Resource Metadata required by the supported client connection flow.

        The metadata shall identify the canonical GHOST MCP resource and the approved authorization server.

        Concrete authorization-provider deployment details remain owned by the deployment requirements.
      • GHOST-MCP-BEARER-TOKEN-TRANSPORT
        3.3. Bearer Token Transport GHOST-MCP-BEARER-TOKEN-TRANSPORT An authenticated MCP client shall present its access token through the HTTP Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.

        Access tokens shall not be accepted through URI query parameters.
      • GHOST-MCP-TOKEN-RESOURCE-VALIDATION
        3.4. Token Validation GHOST-MCP-TOKEN-RESOURCE-VALIDATION Before executing a protected MCP operation, GHOST shall validate the presented token according to the active authorization configuration, including expiration and resource/scope requirements where applicable.

        A token that does not authorize the GHOST MCP resource shall not authorize a GHOST tool call.
      • GHOST-MCP-OWNER-ISOLATION
        3.5. Authenticated Owner Isolation GHOST-MCP-OWNER-ISOLATION Where an MCP capability accesses persistent user-owned state, the authenticated identity shall define the owner scope for that operation.

        The current MCP memory implementation uses the authenticated Cognito subject as owner_sub.

        A memory lookup, list, append, resume, or deletion operation shall not expose or mutate another authenticated owner's persistent data.
      • GHOST-MCP-AUTHENTICATION-FAILURE
        3.6. Authentication Failure Response GHOST-MCP-AUTHENTICATION-FAILURE A protected request without valid authentication shall fail before application-tool execution.

        The failure response shall not reveal access tokens, secrets, internal stack traces, stored memory bodies, prompt contents, or other protected GHOST state.
      • GHOST-MCP-AUTHORIZATION-FAILURE
        3.7. Authorization Failure Response GHOST-MCP-AUTHORIZATION-FAILURE An authenticated request that lacks authorization for the requested MCP operation shall be rejected without executing the tool.
    • GHOST-MCP-MALFORMED-REQUEST-ERROR
      4.3. Malformed MCP Request Error GHOST-MCP-MALFORMED-REQUEST-ERROR Malformed MCP or JSON-RPC requests, unsupported protocol operations, and unknown tool identifiers shall be rejected through the applicable MCP error path before GHOST application functionality executes.
      • GHOST-MCP-ERROR-SANITIZATION
        4.4. Error Information Sanitization GHOST-MCP-ERROR-SANITIZATION Client-visible MCP failures shall provide sufficient information to identify the failed operation without exposing:

        - secrets;
        - bearer tokens;
        - provider credentials;
        - hidden reasoning;
        - internal prompts not intended for output;
        - raw internal model responses;
        - stack traces;
        - protected filesystem details; or
        - another owner's persistent data.
    • GHOST-MCP-PROTOCOL-ACCEPTANCE
      6.1. MCP Protocol Acceptance GHOST-MCP-PROTOCOL-ACCEPTANCE The MCP runtime shall be testable through a complete protocol sequence including:

      1. initialize;
      2. initialized notification where required;
      3. tools/list; and
      4. tools/call for an advertised tool.

      The result shall conform to the declared MCP contract of the selected tool.
      • GHOST-MCP-CHATGPT-ACCEPTANCE
        6.2. ChatGPT End-to-End Acceptance GHOST-MCP-CHATGPT-ACCEPTANCE A deployed GHOST MCP capability intended for ChatGPT shall be verified with the real supported ChatGPT client connection flow.

        Successful local unit testing alone shall not be treated as proof of ChatGPT interoperability.
      • GHOST-MCP-CLAUDE-ACCEPTANCE
        6.3. Claude End-to-End Acceptance GHOST-MCP-CLAUDE-ACCEPTANCE A deployed GHOST MCP capability intended for Claude shall be verified with the real supported Claude client connection flow.

        Successful local unit testing alone shall not be treated as proof of Claude interoperability.
    • GHOST-MCP-EXTENSION-APPROVAL
      7.1. Explicit Approval for MCP Scope Extension GHOST-MCP-EXTENSION-APPROVAL A new MCP capability shall be added only through explicitly approved requirements defining the behavior necessary for that capability.

      The presence of experimental implementation code shall not by itself promote that experiment to a permanent product requirement.
      • GHOST-MCP-CONTRACT-CHANGE-CONTROL
        7.2. MCP Contract Change Control GHOST-MCP-CONTRACT-CHANGE-CONTROL A material change to an approved MCP tool identifier, required input, output semantics, persistence effects, destructive behavior, authorization boundary, or retrieval behavior shall be treated as an MCP interface-contract change.

        The change shall be reflected in approved requirements and corresponding verification before it is treated as the new stable contract.
    • GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT
      1.1. MCP Capability Scope GHOST-MCP-CAP-ROOT GHOST MCP shall support the approved Prompt Engineering capability and three non-ActiveBlackboard memory modes:

      - Episodic Memory;
      - Clipboard Memory; and
      - Collection Memory.

      ActiveBlackboard shall remain separately owned by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
      • GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL
        2.1. GHOST Prompt Engineering Tool GHOST-MCP-ENGINEER-PROMPT-TOOL The MCP server shall expose the GHOST Prompt Engineering capability through the tool identifier:

        ghost_engineer_prompt

        The tool shall use the established GHOST prompt-processing path rather than implement an independent MCP-specific prompt-engineering algorithm.
        • GHOST-MCP-APPROVED-FLOW
          2.2. Prompt Engineering Processing Flow GHOST-MCP-APPROVED-FLOW The stable Prompt Engineering processing path shall:

          1. accept the current prompt text;
          2. create isolated request state;
          3. execute existing deterministic PreProcessing;
          4. execute existing A2 PromptShaper on the resulting SuperPrompt;
          5. rebuild the authoritative prompt-ready representation; and
          6. return the engineered prompt.

          Prompt Engineering shall not independently duplicate PreProcessing or A2 algorithms inside the MCP adapter.
          • GHOST-MCP-FRESH-SUPERPROMPT
            2.3. Fresh Prompt State Per Prompt-Engineering Call GHOST-MCP-FRESH-SUPERPROMPT Each Prompt Engineering call shall operate on request-isolated SuperPrompt state.

            Mutable prompt state from another user, request, or earlier tool call shall not be reused as the active processing state for the new call.
          • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-CALL
            2.4. Existing PreProcessing Reuse GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-CALL The Prompt Engineering adapter shall invoke the existing GHOST deterministic PreProcessing behavior.

            It shall not implement a second MCP-specific parser, canonical-header model, default system, alias model, or prompt normalization algorithm.
            • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-STAGE-GATE
              2.5. PreProcessing Completion Gate GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESS-STAGE-GATE A2 PromptShaper shall execute only after successful completion of the required PreProcessing operation for the same request.

              A failed PreProcessing operation shall not be represented as a successful engineered prompt.
              • GHOST-MCP-A2-CALL
                2.6. Existing A2 PromptShaper Reuse GHOST-MCP-A2-CALL The Prompt Engineering capability shall invoke the established A2 PromptShaper behavior and its existing Agent Stack infrastructure.

                The MCP adapter shall not create a second independent A2 prompt, selector implementation, field-write-back algorithm, or provider-specific A2 pipeline.
                • GHOST-MCP-A2-COMPLETION-GATE
                  2.7. A2 Completion Gate GHOST-MCP-A2-COMPLETION-GATE A successful engineered-prompt result shall be produced only after the required A2 processing and final prompt projection have completed successfully.
                  • GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE
                    2.8. Authoritative Engineered Prompt Source GHOST-MCP-ENGINEERED-PROMPT-SOURCE The engineered prompt returned through MCP shall originate from the authoritative GHOST prompt-ready projection.

                    The MCP adapter shall not independently regenerate or paraphrase that engineered prompt.
        • GHOST-MCP-NO-ANSWER-GENERATION
          2.9. Prompt Engineering Is Not Answer Generation GHOST-MCP-NO-ANSWER-GENERATION The ghost_engineer_prompt operation itself shall remain a prompt-engineering capability.

          Its core GHOST operation shall not be redefined as the application's general final-answer generator.
        • GHOST-MCP-PROMPT-EXPERIMENT-BOUNDARY
          2.10. Experimental Prompt Modes Are Not Stable Requirements GHOST-MCP-PROMPT-EXPERIMENT-BOUNDARY Temporary implementation experiments that alter client behavior around ghost_engineer_prompt, including experimental Prompt:, MEM:, plain-request mode switching or supportive-context routing, shall not become stable product requirements unless separately approved.

          Their temporary presence in source code shall not require preservation in future MCP implementations.
      • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL
        3.1. Four-Mode MCP Memory Model GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL The approved GHOST MCP memory model shall consist of four conceptual memory modes:

        1. Episodic Memory.
        2. Clipboard Memory.
        3. Collection Memory.
        4. ActiveBlackboard Memory.

        This document owns the first three modes.

        ActiveBlackboard is owned exclusively by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-COMMON-TRUTH
          3.2. Common Durable Memory Infrastructure GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-COMMON-TRUTH MCP memory modes may reuse the established GHOST durable-memory infrastructure, including:

          - MemoryRecord;
          - .ragmem durable episode bodies;
          - .ragmeta.json metadata;
          - SQLite indexing; and
          - vector storage where required by the owning memory mode.

          MCP-specific semantics shall not require creation of a second unrelated memory truth model when the common GHOST infrastructure can represent the approved behavior.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE
            3.3. Owner-Scoped Memory GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNER-SCOPE Every persistent MCP memory operation shall be scoped to the authenticated owner.

            An exact key, record ID, Collection ID, Collection Name, Clipboard slot, or other selector shall never bypass owner isolation.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE
          4.1.1. Shared Save Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE GHOST shall expose one clear Save concept for ordinary memory episodes.

          The current executable tool identifier ghost_memory_tag represents the existing implementation of this save concept.

          A future rename of that tool is not approved by this requirement and shall require a separate interface-contract decision.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT
            4.1.2. Save Visible Conversation Content GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-VISIBLE-CONTENT When saving a visible conversation episode, the selected visible user content and corresponding visible assistant content shall be stored without substitution by hidden reasoning, internal tool traffic, or an internal model/tool result.

            When exact visible content is required by the selected Save operation, ChatGPT shall pass that content without summarizing it.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION
            4.1.3. Episode Title and Description GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-TITLE-DESCRIPTION A newly saved ordinary memory episode shall have:

            - an Episode Title; and
            - an Episode Description.

            ChatGPT shall generate both from the selected visible episode unless a more specific mode requirement states otherwise.

            Episode Title is primarily human-facing metadata.

            Episode Description is the compact semantic description used by intelligent Episodic retrieval.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY
            4.1.4. Recall Key Handling and Episodic Uniqueness GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-SAVE-RECALL-KEY When the user explicitly provides a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall pass that key.

            When the user requests an Episodic save without providing a Recall Key, ChatGPT shall generate an appropriate Recall Key rather than forcing the user to invent one.

            Within an authenticated owner's Episodic Memory, the effective Recall Key shall be unique.

            Before saving a new Episodic episode, GHOST shall check the owner-scoped Episodic Recall Keys recorded in the SQLite/index layer.

            If the requested or generated base key is already used by an Episodic episode, GHOST shall deterministically allocate the next available numeric suffix using the form:

            base_key_1
            base_key_2
            base_key_3

            and so on.

            The originally supplied key shall remain the base key; GHOST shall not overwrite the existing episode.

            The successful save result shall return the actual effective Recall Key that was stored.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL
          4.2.1. Shared Recall Concept GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-RECALL GHOST shall expose one Recall concept capable of selecting the appropriate retrieval path from the user's request.

          For Episodic Memory, Recall shall support:

          - deterministic exact retrieval when an exact Recall Key or exact Record ID is known; and
          - intelligent semantic retrieval when the user describes a memory without knowing its exact identifier.

          The two paths access the same Episodic Memory domain.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL
            4.2.2. Exact Recall GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-EXACT-RECALL An exact Recall Key or exact Record ID shall be handled deterministically.

            Exact identifiers shall directly select stored records within the authenticated owner's scope.

            Exact Recall shall not require semantic vector ranking.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER
            4.2.3. Exact Identifiers Are Not Intelligent-Retrieval Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-NO-FAKE-EXACT-FILTER Recall Key and Record ID shall not be treated as approximate SQL narrowing filters for intelligent semantic retrieval.

            When an exact identifier is supplied, GHOST shall use the deterministic exact path.

            When the identifier is unknown, GHOST shall use the intelligent Episodic retrieval path defined in this document.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST
          4.3.1. Shared Memory List GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST ghost_memory_list shall provide metadata discovery and navigation rather than full episode retrieval.

          The shared list capability shall be available for memory modes where listing is meaningful, except Clipboard Memory.

          The list capability may return identifying and descriptive metadata such as:

          - memory or conversation name;
          - memory type;
          - Recall Key;
          - Record ID;
          - Episode Title;
          - Episode Description; and
          - creation time.

          Stored full input/output bodies shall remain Recall content rather than List content.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS
            4.3.2. Deterministic List Filters GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-LIST-FILTERS The shared memory list operation shall support deterministic metadata filtering sufficient for practical discovery.

            Approved filter dimensions include:

            - memory or conversation name;
            - memory type;
            - date range; and
            - deterministic description matching.

            List shall not silently become semantic full-memory retrieval.
        • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE
          4.4.1. Deterministic Memory Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE ghost_memory_delete shall delete individual memory episodes only through an exact selector:

          - exact Recall Key; or
          - exact Record ID.

          Delete shall never use semantic similarity, a natural-language description, Episode Description similarity, vector retrieval, fuzzy matching, or an LLM decision to choose what data to destroy.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY
            4.4.2. Duplicate Recall-Key Safety GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-DUPLICATE-SAFETY If an exact Recall Key resolves to multiple owner-scoped records, GHOST shall not silently choose an arbitrary record for deletion.

            The user shall be given deterministic identifiers sufficient to select the intended episode, or shall explicitly request deletion of all exact matches where that behavior is supported.
          • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD
            4.4.3. Clipboard Excluded from Generic Delete GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-DELETE-NO-CLIPBOARD Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the generic ghost_memory_delete operation.

            Clipboard lifecycle shall be controlled by its dedicated short-retention policy.
        • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT
          5.1. Episodic Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-ROOT Episodic Memory shall store ordinary persistent memory episodes that can later be recovered either:

          - directly through an exact Recall Key or Record ID; or
          - intelligently from a natural-language description.

          Direct Recall and intelligent retrieval shall be two access paths to the same Episodic Memory rather than separate memory types.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED
            5.2. Episode Description Required for Episodic Save GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-REQUIRED Each newly saved Episodic Memory episode shall contain a non-empty Episode Description.

            The description shall summarize the semantic content or useful meaning of that individual episode sufficiently to support later intelligent retrieval.

            The Episode Description shall not be replaced by the Episode Title.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR
              5.3. Episode Description Embedding GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DESCRIPTION-VECTOR The Episode Description shall have a precomputed vector representation available for intelligent Episodic retrieval.

              The description embedding shall be created from the stored Episode Description rather than generated dynamically from the complete episode during every recall.
          • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY
            5.4. Intelligent Recall Query Description GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-INTELLIGENT-QUERY When the user requests a memory without knowing an exact identifier, ChatGPT shall formulate the semantic description of the memory being sought.

            That query description shall be embedded at recall time and compared against stored Episode Description embeddings.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING
              5.5. Optional Date Narrowing GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-DATE-NARROWING Intelligent Episodic retrieval may first apply a deterministic SQL date-range filter when the user's request provides a relevant date or date interval.

              Date range is the approved deterministic narrowing dimension for the intelligent Episodic retrieval path.

              The intelligent path shall not invent key-prefix, title-prefix, or approximate Recall Key filtering as additional narrowing mechanisms.
            • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING
              5.6. Episode Description Similarity Ranking GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-COSINE-RANKING After any optional date narrowing, intelligent Episodic retrieval shall compare the query-description vector with stored Episode Description vectors using cosine similarity or the equivalent cosine-ranking behavior of the selected vector implementation.

              Ranking shall be based primarily on Episode Description semantics.
              • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN
                5.7. Compact Intelligent Recall Candidates GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CANDIDATE-RETURN The intelligent retrieval stage shall return only a small ranked candidate set to the client model.

                The target candidate set shall normally contain approximately five to ten candidates.

                Each candidate shall provide sufficient metadata for selection, including at least:

                - Record ID; and
                - Episode Description.

                The candidate stage shall not return the complete stored Q/A bodies for every candidate.
                • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION
                  5.8. Client Model Candidate Selection GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-CLIENT-SELECTION After receiving the compact ranked candidate descriptions, the invoking AI client may use the user's request and candidate descriptions to select the intended episode.

                  The selection result shall resolve to an exact Record ID before the full episode is fetched.
                  • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH
                    5.9. Exact Final Episode Fetch GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-EXACT-FINAL-FETCH After intelligent candidate selection, GHOST shall fetch the chosen full episode deterministically by exact Record ID.

                    Full episode content shall be loaded only after the candidate-selection step has resolved the exact stored record.
              • GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL
                5.10. No Mandatory Title-First Semantic Funnel GHOST-MCP-EPISODIC-NO-TITLE-FIRST-FUNNEL Episode Title shall remain useful human-facing metadata but shall not be a mandatory first semantic-ranking stage before Episode Description similarity.

                The approved intelligent-retrieval path shall rank Episode Descriptions directly.
        • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT
          6.1. Clipboard Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-ROOT Clipboard Memory shall provide short-lived, deterministic temporary memory slots for lightweight save-and-recall workflows.

          Clipboard Memory shall use the reserved slot identifiers:

          M1 through M100.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS
            6.2. Reserved Clipboard Routing GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RESERVED-KEYS M1 through M100 shall be reserved for Clipboard Memory.

            A normal Episodic save shall not silently store an M1-M100 key as an ordinary Episodic Recall Key.

            When a user explicitly requests saving to or recalling from M1-M100, the request shall be routed to Clipboard Memory behavior.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE
            6.3. One Clipboard File Per Day GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-DAILY-FILE For each authenticated owner, Clipboard Memory shall use at most one Clipboard memory history file for a UTC day in which Clipboard content is saved.

            Clipboard storage shall not perform intra-day file rollover merely because several Clipboard episodes are appended.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY
            6.4. Append-Only Clipboard Storage GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-APPEND-ONLY Clipboard writes shall be append-only.

            Saving to an already used slot shall append a new episode with the same slot identifier rather than physically overwriting the older episode.

            For example, repeated saves to M7 may produce several historical M7 episodes in durable storage.
            • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL
              6.5. Newest Matching Clipboard Recall GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-LATEST-RECALL Recall of a Clipboard slot shall return the newest owner-scoped episode with that exact slot identifier.

              Creation timestamps and deterministic ordering metadata shall be sufficient to identify the newest matching episode.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT
            6.6. Clipboard Episode Content GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-CONTENT A Clipboard episode shall store only the visible saved content and metadata required for deterministic slot storage and recall.

            Clipboard episodes shall not require or generate an Episode Description.

            Clipboard episodes shall not maintain an ActiveBrief.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL
            6.7. Clipboard Uses Exact Slot Recall Only GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-SEMANTIC-RETRIEVAL Clipboard Memory shall not provide intelligent semantic retrieval.

            Clipboard Recall shall use the exact M1-M100 slot identifier and return the newest exact match.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE
            6.8. Clipboard Outside Generic List and Delete GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-NO-GENERIC-LIST-DELETE Clipboard Memory shall not participate in the shared generic memory List or Delete operations.

            The user-facing model shall treat Clipboard as a temporary slot mechanism rather than as a manually administered long-term memory archive.
          • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION
            6.9. Short Clipboard Retention GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-RETENTION Clipboard Memory shall be short-lived.

            The approved default retention window shall be approximately ten days, represented through explicit expiration metadata rather than inferred from a filename.

            Expired Clipboard histories shall be eligible for physical deletion together with their corresponding SQLite index rows.
            • GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP
              6.10. Asynchronous Expired Clipboard Cleanup GHOST-MCP-CLIPBOARD-STARTUP-CLEANUP Expired Clipboard memory cleanup shall run asynchronously during MCP/server startup.

              Startup cleanup shall use authoritative expiration metadata and shall remove expired durable Clipboard files and corresponding index records coherently.
        • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT
          7.1. Collection Memory Scope GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ROOT Collection Memory shall provide a persistent topic-oriented container into which explicitly requested memory episodes can be appended over time.

          A Collection is not an automatically recorded conversation.

          A Collection groups intentionally saved episodes around a user-defined subject or purpose.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT
            7.2. Collection Initialization GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INIT Creating a Collection shall require:

            - Collection Name; and
            - Collection Description or Purpose.

            Initialization shall create a stable Collection identity and shall record its creation time.

            The underlying stable file_id shall serve as the Collection ID.
            • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY
              7.3. Stable Collection Identity GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-IDENTITY Collection ID shall remain stable independently of later episode appends.

              A Collection may be targeted for an append by:

              - exact Collection ID; or
              - exact Collection Name where that name resolves safely within the authenticated owner's scope.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND
            7.4. Collection Append Is Explicit GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EXPLICIT-APPEND A Collection shall receive a new episode only when the user explicitly asks GHOST to save or add content to that Collection.

            Normal conversation turns shall not be appended automatically merely because a Collection exists.
            • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA
              7.5. Collection Episode Description GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-EPISODE-METADATA Every appended Collection episode shall contain an Episode Description describing that episode's local contribution to the Collection.

              A Recall Key may be explicitly supplied or generated according to the shared Save policy.
            • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF
              7.6. Collection Cumulative ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-ACTIVEBRIEF Every appended Collection episode shall also carry the current cumulative Collection ActiveBrief.

              The Collection ActiveBrief shall summarize the accumulated knowledge or state of the Collection's fixed topic after incorporating the new episode.

              The Collection ActiveBrief is not a conversation-summary mechanism and shall not be confused with ActiveBlackboard merely because both use an ActiveBrief concept.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST
            7.7. List Collections GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST GHOST shall support listing Collections for the authenticated owner.

            The Collection list shall provide sufficient metadata for deterministic identification, including at least:

            - Collection ID;
            - Collection Name;
            - Collection Description or Purpose; and
            - creation date.
            • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES
              7.8. List Episodes in a Collection GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-LIST-EPISODES Given an exact Collection ID, GHOST shall support listing the episodes belonging to that Collection.

              The episode list shall return metadata for all Collection episodes, including:

              - Recall Key where present; and
              - Episode Description.

              This operation is metadata navigation and shall not automatically return the complete stored content of every episode.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL
            7.9. Individual Collection Episode Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-RECALL An individual Collection episode shall not require a separate Collection-specific recall mechanism when it has an exact Recall Key or Record ID.

            The shared exact Recall capability shall be used for an individual episode.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL
            7.10. Collection Episode Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-RECALL GHOST shall support Collection-specific retrieval by episode number or episode range.

            Examples include:

            - one episode such as episode 3; or
            - a range such as episodes 2 through 7.

            Episode ordering shall be deterministic within the Collection.
            • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY
              7.11. Token-Safe Collection Range Recall GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-RANGE-TOKEN-SAFETY When a requested Collection range would produce more content than can be returned safely in the active client/model context, GHOST may return a deterministic prefix of the requested range.

              The response shall explicitly identify the unreturned remainder so that the client can request it subsequently.

              The exact token threshold or page size is intentionally not fixed by this requirement.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE
            7.12. Whole Collection Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-WHOLE Deleting an entire Collection shall be a separate destructive operation from deleting an individual memory episode.

            Whole-Collection deletion shall require the exact Collection ID.

            A Collection shall not be destroyed by semantic description, Collection Name similarity, or LLM selection.
            • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION
              7.13. Two-Step Whole Collection Delete Safety GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-DELETE-CONFIRMATION Whole-Collection deletion shall use a temporary server-side confirmation state.

              For an authenticated owner and exact Collection ID, the first exact whole-Collection delete request shall not execute the deletion.

              The first request shall set the corresponding server-side delete-pending state to true and shall return a warning or refusal asking the client/user to repeat the same exact Collection deletion request.

              If the same owner repeats the exact whole-Collection delete request for the same Collection ID while that delete-pending state is true, GHOST shall execute the deletion and confirm the result.

              The delete-pending state shall be volatile server state and shall reset to false when the MCP server restarts.

              A future timeout or asynchronous reset policy may be added later, but no timeout duration or additional reset mechanism is fixed by this requirement.
          • GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE
            7.14. Individual Collection Episode Delete GHOST-MCP-COLLECTION-INDIVIDUAL-DELETE Deleting an individual episode from a Collection shall use the shared deterministic memory Delete behavior.

            No separate Collection-specific single-episode deletion contract is required.
      • GHOST-MCP-CAP-NO-IMPLEMENTATION-INVENTION
        8.1. No False Implementation Claim GHOST-MCP-CAP-NO-IMPLEMENTATION-INVENTION A requirement in this document shall not be reported as currently implemented solely because underlying data fields or partial infrastructure already exist.

        Implementation status shall require corresponding executable behavior and verification.
    • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-ROOT
      1.1. ActiveBlackboard Scope GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-ROOT GHOST shall maintain a dedicated MCP requirement area for ActiveBlackboard.

      The requirement area shall distinguish:

      - current Persistent Chat behavior that already exists; and
      - future shared ActiveBlackboard behavior that remains under design.
      • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-CURRENT-PROTOTYPE
        2.1. Persistent Chat as ActiveBlackboard Prototype GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-CURRENT-PROTOTYPE The current Persistent Chat implementation shall be treated as the first executable ActiveBlackboard prototype.

        It validates:

        - explicit activation of persistent conversation recording;
        - one persistent history across multiple conversation turns;
        - append-only visible Q/A recording;
        - cumulative ActiveBrief continuity;
        - deterministic resume; and
        - owner-scoped persistent state.

        It shall not be represented as the final multi-actor ActiveBlackboard architecture.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-CURRENT-SINGLE-STREAM
          2.2. Current Single-Stream Boundary GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-CURRENT-SINGLE-STREAM The current Persistent Chat implementation shall be treated as a single continuing chat stream.

          Its use of ActiveBlackboard-related storage naming shall not by itself establish implemented multi-chat, multi-actor, shared-board, or agent-coordination behavior.
        • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-TOOL
          3.1. Persistent Chat Initialize Tool GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-TOOL The current MCP server shall expose:

          ghost_persistent_chat_init

          Initialization shall explicitly create one new persistent chat memory for the authenticated owner.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-EXPLICIT
            3.2. Persistent Recording Requires Explicit Activation GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-EXPLICIT Persistent Chat recording shall begin only after an explicit successful initialization or resume operation.

            Ordinary conversation before activation shall not be represented as automatically persisted by this capability.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-INPUT
            3.3. Initialization Identity GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-INPUT Initialization shall require a user-provided title.

            A general memory description may also be supplied.

            The implementation shall not invent unsupported project facts merely to populate an optional description.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-STABLE-ID
            3.4. Stable Persistent Memory Identity GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-STABLE-ID Initialization shall create one stable persistent memory identity.

            The current implementation exposes this identity as file_id.

            The same persistent memory shall continue across dates and later resume operations rather than being split into a new daily conversation memory.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-NO-EPISODE
            3.5. Initialization Does Not Save a Conversation Episode GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-INIT-NO-EPISODE Initialization shall create the persistent memory history but shall not fabricate or save a conversation episode.

            The first episode shall be created only by a subsequent successful append.
        • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-APPEND-TOOL
          4.1. Persistent Chat Append Tool GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-APPEND-TOOL The current MCP server shall expose:

          ghost_persistent_chat_append

          The operation shall append one normal visible user/assistant exchange to an already initialized persistent chat memory.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-VISIBLE-QA
            4.2. Persist Complete Visible Q/A GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-VISIBLE-QA Each appended episode shall contain:

            - the complete visible user message; and
            - the substantive visible assistant answer produced for that user message.

            The persistence path shall not intentionally replace the visible exchange with a summary.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-NO-HIDDEN-CONTENT
              4.3. Hidden Processing Is Not Conversation Content GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-NO-HIDDEN-CONTENT Persistent Chat shall not save as conversation content:

              - hidden chain-of-thought;
              - internal model reasoning;
              - MCP protocol traffic;
              - internal tool results;
              - hidden tool arguments;
              - internal application diagnostics; or
              - the GHOST persistence receipt itself.

              Only the visible conversation content selected by the approved append behavior shall form the saved Q/A episode.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-PRESENTATION-AUTHORITY
              4.4. Client Remains Answer Presentation Authority GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-PRESENTATION-AUTHORITY The invoking AI client shall compose the normal complete answer for the user before that answer is persisted.

              GHOST Persistent Chat shall store the supplied answer and shall not become a replacement answer renderer.

              Normal Markdown, code blocks, tables, and other visible answer formatting may remain part of the persisted assistant response.
              • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-ANSWER-BEFORE-APPEND
                4.5. Answer Then Persist GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-ANSWER-BEFORE-APPEND The intended visible interaction order shall be:

                1. compose the normal assistant answer;
                2. append the same substantive visible Q/A to Persistent Chat;
                3. receive the GHOST save result; and
                4. present the normal answer followed by the short persistence receipt when appropriate.

                The persistence receipt shall not become part of the saved assistant answer.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-APPEND-EXISTING-ONLY
            4.6. Append Does Not Create Missing Persistent Memory GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-APPEND-EXISTING-ONLY ghost_persistent_chat_append shall operate only on an existing owner-scoped Persistent Chat memory.

            Append failure shall not silently initialize a new persistent memory.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-ACTIVEBRIEF
            5.1. Cumulative ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-ACTIVEBRIEF Each successfully appended Persistent Chat episode shall contain the current cumulative ActiveBrief.

            The ActiveBrief shall represent the useful cumulative conversation state required to continue the persistent chat.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-FIRST-BRIEF
              5.2. Initial ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-FIRST-BRIEF For the first persisted episode, the invoking AI client shall compose the initial ActiveBrief from that first visible Q/A.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-BRIEF-UPDATE
              5.3. ActiveBrief Update GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-BRIEF-UPDATE For each later episode, the invoking AI client shall construct the updated cumulative ActiveBrief from:

              - the previous latest ActiveBrief; and
              - the current visible user/assistant exchange.

              The resulting ActiveBrief shall represent the updated cumulative state after the new episode.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-CLIENT-BRIEF-AUTHORITY
              5.4. Client-Composed ActiveBrief GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-CLIENT-BRIEF-AUTHORITY The current Persistent Chat prototype shall rely on the invoking AI client to compose the updated ActiveBrief.

              GHOST persistence code shall store the supplied ActiveBrief and shall not require a separate GHOST LLM call merely to recreate the same cumulative summary.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-SEQUENCE
            6.1. Persistent Episode Sequence GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-SEQUENCE Each appended Persistent Chat episode shall have deterministic sequence ordering within its persistent memory.

            The current implementation stores sequence_number and links a new episode to the preceding episode through parent_id.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-STREAM-ID
              6.2. Persistent Chat Stream Identity GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-STREAM-ID Current Persistent Chat episodes shall remain traceable to their persistent stream.

              The current implementation stores the stable persistent file_id as the chat_stream_id for appended episodes.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RECORD-ID
            6.3. Stable Episode Record ID GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RECORD-ID Each persisted episode shall have a stable Record ID.

            The Record ID shall be returned in the successful persistence receipt and shall remain usable as an exact handle for deterministic resume.
        • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-COMMON-PERSISTENCE
          6.4. Common GHOST Persistence Infrastructure GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-COMMON-PERSISTENCE The current Persistent Chat implementation shall use the established GHOST durable memory infrastructure:

          - MemoryRecord;
          - .ragmem;
          - .ragmeta.json;
          - shared SQLite indexing; and
          - stable file_id / record_id identities.

          Persistent Chat shall not require a parallel unrelated persistence format.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-COHERENCE
            6.5. Body Metadata and Index Coherence GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-COHERENCE Before continuing or resuming an existing Persistent Chat memory, the current implementation shall validate coherence among the durable memory body, metadata file, and SQLite index sufficiently to avoid continuing from an inconsistent identity or episode set.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-PARTIAL-SAVE
            6.6. Partial Save Shall Not Be Reported as Success GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-PARTIAL-SAVE If durable episode body data has been written but a later metadata or SQLite update fails, GHOST shall not claim that the episode was coherently saved.

            The failure result may identify the durable Record ID so recovery or repair remains possible.
        • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-TOOL
          7.1. Persistent Chat Resume Tool GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-TOOL The current MCP server shall expose:

          ghost_persistent_chat_resume

          Resume shall locate an existing owner-scoped Persistent Chat memory through an exact previously persisted episode Record ID.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-NO-CREATE
            7.2. Resume Never Creates a Memory GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-NO-CREATE A failed resume request shall not initialize or fabricate a new Persistent Chat memory.

            Resume is a deterministic recovery operation over already existing persistent state.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-OWNER
            7.3. Owner-Scoped Resume GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-OWNER A Record ID used for resume shall resolve only within the authenticated owner's Persistent Chat memories.

            A Record ID belonging to another owner shall not expose or resume that owner's persistent memory.
          • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-LATEST
            7.4. Resume From Latest Coherent State GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-LATEST The supplied Record ID shall identify the Persistent Chat history.

            After that history is identified, continuation shall use the latest coherent episode and latest cumulative ActiveBrief belonging to that history, even when newer episodes exist after the supplied resume handle.
            • GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-STATE
              7.5. Resume State GHOST-MCP-PCHAT-RESUME-STATE A successful resume shall provide sufficient state for continued persistence, including:

              - stable persistent file_id;
              - title;
              - description where present;
              - latest Record ID;
              - latest sequence number;
              - latest episode time; and
              - latest cumulative ActiveBrief.

              The exact current response schema may additionally expose related metadata already present in the implementation.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-NO-CURRENT-MULTIACTOR
          9.1. No Current Multi-Actor Blackboard Claim GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-NO-CURRENT-MULTIACTOR The current Persistent Chat prototype shall not be represented as implementing:

          - several cooperating actor streams;
          - autonomous Blackboard agents;
          - Programmer/Auditor/Architect/Requirements coordination;
          - shared multi-chat routing;
          - background Blackboard orchestration; or
          - a completed shared-board GUI.

          Those capabilities belong to the future ActiveBlackboard vision.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-NO-INVENTED-CURRENT-TOOLS
          9.2. No Invented Current Lifecycle Tools GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-NO-INVENTED-CURRENT-TOOLS Current implementation documentation shall identify the executable Persistent Chat tools as Init, Append, and Resume.

          Verify, Close, actor-routing, board-synchronization, or other hypothetical lifecycle tools shall not be claimed as implemented unless corresponding code and requirements are later approved.
      • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-LIST-TARGET
        8.1. ActiveBlackboard Participation in Generic List GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-LIST-TARGET ActiveBlackboard memories shall participate in the shared generic memory List capability when that capability is extended to the final memory model.

        List shall expose metadata and navigation information rather than automatically returning complete persistent-chat histories.
      • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-EPISODE-DELETE
        8.2. Individual ActiveBlackboard Episode Delete GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-EPISODE-DELETE An individual ActiveBlackboard/Persistent Chat episode may be deleted through the shared deterministic memory Delete capability using an exact Record ID or other approved exact selector.

        Semantic or descriptive deletion shall not be used.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-DELETE-BRIEF-TRACE
          8.3. ActiveBrief Residual Trace After Episode Delete GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-DELETE-BRIEF-TRACE Deleting an individual historical ActiveBlackboard episode does not require rewriting all later cumulative ActiveBriefs.

          A later ActiveBrief may therefore preserve a summarized trace of information that originated in the deleted episode.

          This residual cumulative-summary effect is accepted for individual episode deletion.
      • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-SHARED
        10.1. Shared Ongoing Blackboard GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-SHARED A future ActiveBlackboard shall support ongoing shared work context spanning more than one participating chat or specialist actor.

        The Blackboard shall provide durable continuity so participating actors can work from shared project state rather than depending solely on one native client conversation.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-ACTORS
          10.2. Multiple Specialist Actors GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-ACTORS Future ActiveBlackboard participants may include specialist roles such as:

          - Programmer;
          - Auditor;
          - Architect;
          - Requirements; and
          - other explicitly defined actors.

          Actor roles shall remain identifiable so their contributions can be inspected and traced.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-BRIEFS
          10.3. Future Actor or Stream ActiveBriefs GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-BRIEFS A future ActiveBlackboard may maintain cumulative ActiveBrief state for individual actors, chat streams, or another explicitly designed Blackboard scope.

          The final rule for shared versus per-actor versus per-stream ActiveBriefs is not yet approved and shall not be invented by this requirement.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-PULL
          10.4. Pull-Based Shared Context Direction GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-PULL The approved future direction favors actors retrieving relevant shared Blackboard state when needed rather than assuming uncontrolled automatic broadcast of all state to all actors.

          The exact retrieval and routing algorithm remains unresolved.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-GUI
          10.5. Future Blackboard Workbench GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-GUI A future GHOST workbench may provide a Blackboard-oriented view of:

          - sessions;
          - streams;
          - actors;
          - titles;
          - timestamps;
          - saved episodes; and
          - relevant cumulative state.

          The workbench direction may support human-controlled filtering, searching, editing, tagging, archiving, and movement of information between appropriate contexts.

          Detailed GUI implementation remains outside the current MCP protocol contract.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-HUMAN-CONTROL
          10.6. Human-Controlled Blackboard GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-FUTURE-HUMAN-CONTROL The future ActiveBlackboard shall remain inspectable and under human control.

          Shared state, actor participation, persistence, and future coordination shall not become an opaque autonomous source of authority over the user's current request.
      • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-UNRESOLVED
        11.1. ActiveBlackboard Detailed Architecture Is Open GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-UNRESOLVED The following future ActiveBlackboard decisions are intentionally unresolved:

        - exact actor coordination protocol;
        - exact actor-routing algorithm;
        - shared versus per-actor versus per-stream ActiveBrief ownership;
        - final Blackboard lifecycle operations;
        - automatic versus user-triggered synchronization;
        - exact shared-state selection semantics;
        - exact conflict-handling behavior;
        - final future MCP tool schemas; and
        - final future GUI interaction model.

        These details shall not be invented in requirements until explicitly designed and approved.
        • GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-NO-FUTURE-IMPLEMENTATION-CLAIM
          11.2. Future Vision Is Not Current Implementation GHOST-MCP-BLACKBOARD-NO-FUTURE-IMPLEMENTATION-CLAIM The existence of the working Persistent Chat prototype shall not be used as evidence that the unresolved multi-chat or multi-actor ActiveBlackboard vision has already been implemented.

          Current implementation claims shall remain limited to verified Persistent Chat behavior.
    • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ROOT
      1.1. Runtime-Control MCP Capability GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ROOT GHOST shall expose an authenticated MCP runtime-control capability through which the user can start the designated GHOST EC2 runtime, inspect its current state, and stop it.

      The runtime-control capability shall remain operational independently of the EC2-hosted GHOST MCP service that it controls.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-SEPARATE-ENDPOINT
        1.2. Separate Always-Available Runtime-Control Endpoint GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-SEPARATE-ENDPOINT Runtime-control tools shall be exposed by an MCP endpoint whose execution path does not depend on the managed GHOST EC2 instance being running.

        The runtime-control endpoint shall therefore remain callable while the managed GHOST EC2 instance is stopped.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-TOOLS
        2.1. Runtime-Control Tool Inventory GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-TOOLS The runtime-control MCP endpoint shall expose exactly the following approved lifecycle tools unless this requirement is later revised:

        - ghost_ec2_start
        - ghost_ec2_status
        - ghost_ec2_stop

        The runtime-control endpoint shall not expose arbitrary general-purpose AWS administration tools.
        • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-TOOL
          3.1. EC2 Start Tool GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-TOOL The runtime-control endpoint shall expose:

          ghost_ec2_start

          The operation shall start the configured GHOST EC2 instance from the stopped state using the selected approved runtime profile and effective idle timeout.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-PROFILE-INPUT
            3.2. Start Runtime Profile Input GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-PROFILE-INPUT ghost_ec2_start shall accept an optional runtime profile selector with exactly the following approved values:

            1. Profile 1: t3.medium.
            2. Profile 2: m7i-flex.xlarge.

            When the user does not provide a runtime profile, the tool shall use Profile 1.

            A runtime profile value other than 1 or 2 shall not select another EC2 instance type.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-IDLE-INPUT
            3.3. Start Idle Timeout Input GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-IDLE-INPUT ghost_ec2_start shall accept an optional idle timeout in minutes.

            When the user does not provide a value, the effective timeout shall be 20 minutes.

            The effective timeout shall be constrained to the range 10 through 120 minutes inclusive. A requested value below 10 shall result in an effective value of 10 minutes, and a requested value above 120 shall result in an effective value of 120 minutes.

            The tool result shall state the effective timeout actually applied.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-STOPPED-ONLY
            3.4. Start Uses Stopped-Instance Configuration GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-STOPPED-ONLY The normal ghost_ec2_start workflow shall assume the managed EC2 instance is stopped.

            While the instance is stopped, the controller shall apply the selected approved instance type and then start the same instance.

            If the instance is not stopped, ghost_ec2_start shall not silently stop or restart it merely to satisfy a different runtime-profile request. The tool shall instead return the observed state and a clear non-ready or no-change result as appropriate.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-READINESS
            3.5. Start Waits for GHOST Readiness GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-READINESS ghost_ec2_start shall not complete with ready=true solely because AWS reports the EC2 instance as running.

            The operation shall wait through the bounded startup sequence until the actual GHOST service health check succeeds or startup readiness fails.

            A failed or timed-out readiness check shall be returned as not ready and shall not be represented as successful startup readiness.
            • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-RESULT
              3.6. Start Result Contract GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-START-RESULT A successful ghost_ec2_start result shall identify at least:

              - the observed EC2 state;
              - the selected runtime profile;
              - the concrete EC2 instance type;
              - the effective idle timeout; and
              - whether GHOST readiness was successfully verified.

              The result shall make the applied profile and timeout explicit so the user does not need to infer them from defaults.
            • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-NO-FALSE-READY
              7.1. No False Ready Result GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-NO-FALSE-READY A runtime-control operation shall not report GHOST as ready when the readiness health verification has not succeeded.

              AWS running state, Docker startup activity, or an attempted health request alone shall not be represented as successful GHOST readiness.
        • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STATUS-TOOL
          4.1. EC2 Status Tool GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STATUS-TOOL The runtime-control endpoint shall expose:

          ghost_ec2_status

          The operation shall inspect the configured GHOST EC2 runtime without starting or stopping it.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STATUS-RESULT
            4.2. Runtime Status Result GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STATUS-RESULT When the information is available, ghost_ec2_status shall report:

            - current EC2 state;
            - current approved runtime profile or concrete instance type;
            - GHOST readiness state when the instance is running;
            - effective idle timeout for the current run; and
            - elapsed time since the latest qualifying GHOST MCP activity.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STATUS-NO-ACTIVITY
            4.3. Status Does Not Keep EC2 Alive GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STATUS-NO-ACTIVITY Calling ghost_ec2_status shall not refresh the managed EC2 instance's GHOST inactivity timer.

            Repeated status polling shall therefore not prevent the inactivity watchdogs from stopping an otherwise unused instance.
        • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STOP-TOOL
          5.1. EC2 Stop Tool GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STOP-TOOL The runtime-control endpoint shall expose:

          ghost_ec2_stop

          The operation shall request a normal stop of the configured GHOST EC2 instance.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STOP-SAFE
            5.2. Safe and Idempotent Stop Behavior GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-STOP-SAFE ghost_ec2_stop shall be safe to call when the managed instance is already stopped and shall not terminate the EC2 instance.

            The stop tool shall not change the configured runtime profile as a side effect of stopping the instance.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-AUTH
        2.2. Runtime-Control Authentication GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-AUTH Every runtime-control tool invocation shall require successful authentication through the approved GHOST Cognito identity environment and shall follow the common MCP authentication and authorization contract owned by 110_mcp.sdoc.

        The existing approved GHOST Cognito user identity shall be usable for the runtime-control endpoint; the capability shall not require a second end-user account solely for EC2 control.

        An unauthenticated caller shall not be able to invoke start, status, or stop.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-FIXED-TARGET
        2.3. Fixed Managed EC2 Target GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-FIXED-TARGET The runtime-control tool interface shall target only the configured GHOST EC2 instance.

        The tools shall not accept an arbitrary EC2 instance ID or other caller-selected AWS resource identifier.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-IDLE-POLICY
        6.1. Per-Run Idle Shutdown Policy GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-IDLE-POLICY Every successful EC2 start shall establish one effective idle timeout for that run.

        If no qualifying GHOST MCP activity occurs for the effective timeout and no qualifying MCP tool call is still executing, the managed EC2 instance shall be stopped by the runtime-control watchdog design defined in 81_aws_deployment_and_operations.sdoc.
        • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ACTIVITY-DEFINITION
          6.2. Qualifying Activity Is an Authenticated GHOST Tool Call GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ACTIVITY-DEFINITION A qualifying activity shall be a real authenticated tools/call invocation accepted for execution by the EC2-hosted GHOST MCP service.

          Examples include approved prompt-engineering, retrieval, memory, Blackboard, and other GHOST functional tool calls executed on the managed EC2 runtime.
          • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ACTIVITY-EXCLUSIONS
            6.3. Background and Control Traffic Is Not Qualifying Activity GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ACTIVITY-EXCLUSIONS The following shall not refresh the GHOST inactivity timer merely by occurring:

            - GHOST health checks;
            - startup readiness polling;
            - OAuth or discovery traffic;
            - MCP initialization;
            - tools/list;
            - ghost_ec2_status polling;
            - watchdog execution;
            - Docker activity;
            - operating-system activity;
            - CPU usage;
            - unrelated network background traffic; or
            - other activity that is not an authenticated GHOST functional tools/call invocation on the managed EC2 runtime.
        • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-INFLIGHT
          6.4. Active Tool Calls Prevent Idle Shutdown GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-INFLIGHT The runtime-control inactivity mechanism shall not stop the EC2 instance while a qualifying authenticated GHOST MCP tool call is actively executing.

          The post-call idle period shall begin from the refreshed completion activity time after the final active qualifying call completes.
        • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-REDUNDANT-WATCHDOG
          6.5. Redundant Idle-Shutdown Enforcement GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-REDUNDANT-WATCHDOG The inactivity policy shall be enforced by both:

          1. a serverless AWS watchdog; and
          2. an independent EC2-local watchdog.

          The local watchdog shall remain capable of stopping an idle run when the Lambda watchdog execution path is unavailable.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-NO-ARBITRARY-AWS
        7.2. No General AWS Control Surface GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-NO-ARBITRARY-AWS The runtime-control MCP capability shall remain limited to the approved GHOST EC2 lifecycle operations and approved runtime profiles.

        It shall not become a generic MCP interface for arbitrary AWS resources, arbitrary instance types, EC2 termination, IAM modification, security-group modification, or other unrelated cloud-administration actions.
      • GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ACCEPTANCE
        8.1. Runtime-Control MCP Acceptance GHOST-MCP-RUNTIME-ACCEPTANCE The runtime-control capability shall not be treated as implemented until acceptance demonstrates at least that:

        1. the runtime-control MCP endpoint remains callable while the managed GHOST EC2 instance is stopped;
        2. unauthenticated control invocations are rejected;
        3. ghost_ec2_start with no optional values selects Profile 1 t3.medium and a 20-minute effective idle timeout;
        4. ghost_ec2_start can select Profile 2 m7i-flex.xlarge while the same EC2 instance is stopped;
        5. the effective idle timeout remains within 10 through 120 minutes;
        6. ghost_ec2_start reports ready only after actual GHOST health verification succeeds;
        7. ghost_ec2_status reports state without resetting idle activity;
        8. ghost_ec2_stop stops but does not terminate the managed EC2 instance;
        9. real authenticated EC2-hosted GHOST tools/call activity refreshes the idle timer;
        10. health checks, polling, and background activity do not refresh the idle timer;
        11. the serverless watchdog stops the instance after qualifying inactivity; and
        12. the EC2-local watchdog independently stops the instance after qualifying inactivity when the serverless watchdog path is unavailable.
    • GHOST-MCP-ROOT

      The MCP capability shall provide a controlled external boundary around approved GHOST functions without transferring ownership of those functions to the MCP transport layer.

      MCP shall be represented as its own capability family in the GHOST requirement hierarchy.

    1. 111_mcp_capabilities.sdoc for all approved MCP capabilities except ActiveBlackboard.
    2. 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc for all current and future ActiveBlackboard behavior.
    3. 113_mcp_runtime_control.sdoc for MCP-visible GHOST runtime life

    GHOST-MCP-INTERFACE-OWNERSHIP
    1.3. MCP Interface Ownership GHOST-MCP-INTERFACE-OWNERSHIP The MCP parent capability shall own:

    - external MCP protocol behavior;
    - MCP transport requirements;
    - MCP capability negotiation;
    - tool discovery and invocation rules;
    - authenticated caller identity;
    - authorization enforcement;
    - common tool-call rate limiting;
    - interface-visible errors;
    - cross-client interoperability;
    - shared MCP security boundaries; and
    - the boundary between MCP functionality and runtime/deployment realization.

    The MCP parent capability shall not duplicate the internal algorithms of Prompt Engineering, Memory Management, ActiveBlackboard, or other GHOST functional subsystems.
    • GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESSING-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE
      5.1. Prompt Processing Ownership Boundary GHOST-MCP-PREPROCESSING-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE The existing GHOST Prompt Engineering capability shall reuse the owning PreProcessing, PromptShaper, Agent Stack, SuperPrompt, and projection behavior rather than implementing duplicate prompt-processing algorithms inside the MCP transport layer.

      Detailed Prompt Engineering MCP behavior is owned by 111_mcp_capabilities.sdoc.
    • GHOST-MCP-AWS-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE
      5.2. Runtime and Deployment Ownership Boundary GHOST-MCP-AWS-OWNERSHIP-REFERENCE Runtime Platform and Operations requirements shall remain responsible for:

      - local runtime realization;
      - AWS runtime realization;
      - container execution;
      - image delivery;
      - public endpoint realization;
      - HTTPS termination;
      - reverse proxy;
      - DNS;
      - authorization-provider deployment;
      - secrets delivery;
      - process startup and restart;
      - persistent deployment paths; and
      - operational verification.

      This MCP requirement family shall define what the MCP capability must do, while the 80-series requirement family shall define how the supported runtime environments deploy and operate it.
    • GHOST-MCP-UI-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY
      5.3. Human Interface Boundary GHOST-MCP-UI-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY The MCP service shall not own the native ChatGPT or Claude user interface.

      The Streamlit and future React/FastAPI interfaces remain separate GHOST interface capabilities.

      An MCP result may be rendered by the invoking client without transferring ownership of the native client UI to GHOST.
    • GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY
      5.4. Memory Infrastructure Ownership Boundary GHOST-MCP-MEMORY-OWNERSHIP-BOUNDARY MCP memory capabilities may use the common GHOST MemoryRecord, .ragmem, .ragmeta.json, SQLite, vector, and memory-management infrastructure.

      The MCP capability requirements shall define MCP-specific memory semantics without redefining unrelated GUI memory-pipeline behavior.

      Where existing Memory Management requirements remain applicable, they shall remain authoritative for their existing scope.

    2.2. ChatGPT and Claude Compatibility GHOST-MCP-CLIENT-COMPATIBILITY The same GHOST MCP service contract shall be usable by approved ChatGPT and Claude MCP client integrations.

    Core GHOST semantics shall not change merely because the invoking client is ChatGPT rather than Claude.

    Client-specific user-interface behavior, connector configuration, or authentication setup may differ without creating different GHOST functional contracts.
    • GHOST-MCP-EXPLICIT-CLIENT-INVOCATION
      2.3. Explicit Client Invocation Boundary GHOST-MCP-EXPLICIT-CLIENT-INVOCATION A GHOST MCP operation shall execute only when the client issues the corresponding MCP request.

      Enabling a GHOST connector or plugin shall not by itself authorize GHOST to treat every ordinary client message as an MCP operation.
    • GHOST-MCP-CROSS-CLIENT-CONSISTENCY

      Client-specific presentation or connection details shall not create different persistence, retrieval, deletion, or prompt-engineering semantics.
